paper_metadata.title: H-EFT-VA: An Effective-Field-Theory Variational Ansatz with Provable Barren Plateau Avoidance

summary: The paper introduces H-EFT-VA, a variational ansatz for TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ ground-state estimation, and reports 109x better energy convergence (-12.00 vs -0.11) and 10.7x higher ground-state fidelity (0.2646 vs 0.0247) than a hardware-efficient ansatz. It also reports gradient-variance scaling of 0.5187 versus ~1e-16 for the baseline, with noisy-simulation benchmarks up to N=14 qubits, L=14 layers, and 1000 shots, but no end-to-end quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Benchmarking H-EFT-VA against a hardware-efficient ansatz on transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) and Heisenberg XXZ Hamiltonians under noiseless and depolarizing-noise simulation, including gradient-variance scaling, convergence, noise robustness, entanglement, purity, fidelity, and parameter-efficiency tests.

algorithm.variant: H-EFT Variational Ansatz (H-EFT-VA) vs hardware-efficient ansatz baseline
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient variational ansatz with hierarchical EFT-inspired small-parameter initialization
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Gaussian prior with small scale; parameters initialized as coupling-like constants with θ ~ N(0, σ^2), σ = κ/(L·N); appendix also states θ_{l,f,c} = α_{l,f,c} c_f with α ~ N(0, σ_init^2), σ_init ≪ 1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Variational circuit for Hamiltonian ground-state preparation; no explicit binary-variable/QUBO encoding described
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize expectation value ⟨H⟩ for TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ Hamiltonians; also evaluate ground-state fidelity and gradient variance
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Transverse Field Ising Model (TFIM) and Heisenberg XXZ Hamiltonians

problem_instance.description: Ground-state estimation for spin-chain Hamiltonians with varying qubit counts and circuit depths

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: TFIM and Heisenberg XXZ benchmark Hamiltonians

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 16 benchmark tests; scalability over N=4,6,8,12,14 and L=2..14; comparisons against HEA; statistical significance reported with p-values; noise and shot robustness evaluated; optimizer robustness tested across Adam/SGD/RMSProp

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: H-EFT-VA converges while HEA stagnates for larger N; noise and shot robustness preserved

speedup_claims.baseline_method: hardware_efficient_ansatz / generic random initialization leading to barren plateaus
speedup_claims.conditions: small-parameter initialization with sigma = kappa/(L·N) and circuits remaining localized near the identity
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a lower bound on gradient variance, not an end-to-end runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: energy convergence at N = 12 in noiseless simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as final energy -12.00 vs -0.11; improvement is problem- and metric-specific.
Reported fidelity values are 0.2646 vs 0.0247; no confidence interval or run count given.

speedup_claims.conditions: No end-to-end quantum advantage or runtime speedup is claimed
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states no asymptotic end-to-end algorithmic speedup is claimed.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Provable gradient-variance lower bound Ω(1/poly(N)) for the ansatz; no end-to-end algorithmic speedup claimed

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; benchmarks only up to N=14 in simulation.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant or at least hardware-validated implementation; current evidence is limited to noisy simulation with 14 qubits and 1000 shots.
